anna_ml: Proposing a new 'StructBot' canary + retry playbook for onboarding quantized models that will be used for funcalls. TL;DR: two-mode canary (strict-parse, soft-parse-with-repair), routing ramp, retry-budget limits, and automatic fallback/rollback. Thoughts?
kevin_infra: +1. Can we run on a dedicated canary pool? Need rough capacity estimate and infra steps.
maria_eval: Agree with structured approach. Suggested guardrails: parse_success (strict) >= 99.5% on seeded prompt set, and soft-parse acceptance (heuristic repairs) F1 >= 98%. Sample plan: 10k canary calls/day with a mix of seed/evasive prompts.
sam_sre: One more thing — protect against retry storms. Add circuit-breaker: max 5% retries per minute per model, global cap 2% of total requests. Also emit a metric for retry spike. :warning:
ci-bot: New PR opened: https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/4923 — structbot playbook and canary manifests.
kevin_infra: infra notes: provision canary pool `canary-small` (3 replicas, mixed gpus) and tag image `structbot-v1`. Example command: `infra canary create --pool=canary-small --tag=structbot-v1 --replicas=3 --route=10%`
maria_eval: Statistical test: do a one-sided proportion z-test vs baseline parse_success; require p < 0.001 for non-inferiority with margin 0.3%. Also track latency P95 and tail-of-token-time to catch quant artifacts.
anna_ml: (typo) anna_ml: Also add two automated healing actions: 1) if strict parse < threshold, flip to soft-parse for 15m and alert, 2) if downstream tool error rate > 0.5% or parse-success stays low after 3 retries, rollback model.
kevin_infra: routing ramp: start at 5-10% traffic, step +10% every 6 hours if no alerts. Add canary tag in request headers: `x-canary: structbot-v1`.
maria_eval: Important: include function-call payload size buckets in telemetry. Quantized models sometimes trim suffixes causing truncated JSON or missing closing braces. Track suffix-truncation-rate.
anna_ml: Example minimal canary invocation + parse-check script (pseudo):
```bash
# send test payloads (seeds + fuzz)
for f in seeds/*.json; do
  http POST $REDCON_API/invoke model=structbot-v1 payload=@$f headers:{"x-canary":"structbot-v1"} | jq -r '.response' > /tmp/out
  # simple parse check
  python tools/parse_check.py /tmp/out || echo "PARSE_FAIL $f"
done
```
And a tiny repair heuristic we run in soft-parse mode:
```python
# pseudo-repair: try json.loads, on failure try wrap in array or append closing brace
import json
def repair(text):
    try:
        return json.loads(text)
    except Exception:
        t = text.strip()
        if t.endswith(','):
            t = t[:-1] + '}'
        if not t.startswith('{') and t.startswith('['):
            t = '[' + t + ']'
        # last-resort: ndjson -> take first valid object
        for line in t.splitlines():
            try:
                return json.loads(line)
            except Exception:
                continue
        raise
```
maria_eval: That repair heuristic is ok for soft-parse but we must label repaired responses and exclude them from strict-success metrics. Also add human review samples for repaired items (1 per 1000).
sam_sre: Alerting: page if parse_success drops by >0.5% absolute vs baseline AND downstream tool errors > 0.2% for 10 minutes. Otherwise just slack alert to #eng-ml-canaries.
kevin_infra: Ops checklist for rollout: infra PR + canary manifest (ci-bot link), dashboard (new grafana rows), k8s HPA tweak for canary pool, and traffic-shift automation. I can own infra bits if @anna_ml + @maria_eval finalize metrics.
anna_ml: I'll draft the playbook doc: steps, metrics, rollback criteria, sample scripts, and a template incident runbook for canary failures. Target to ship draft by EOD tomorrow.
ci-bot: CI checks passed for PR #4923 (unit + integration). :white_check_mark:
maria_eval: I'll prepare the seed set and stat tests, and a small eval harness that computes parse success, repair rate, latency, and downstream tool error correlation.
sam_sre: ok — once draft is up, I'll schedule a 30m sync to review limits and paging.
anna_ml: Great — assigning owners: anna_ml (playbook + rollout), kevin_infra (infra), maria_eval (metrics + eval harness), sam_sre (alerting/paging). I'll follow up with the doc link here when ready. :rocket:
